rafa release tag — tag the commit that set the version both release files agree
  on

Usage:
  rafa release tag [--push]

Description:
  Writes `v<version>` on the release branch — `pr.base`, or `main` — when the
  version `release.versionFile` declares is the one the newest section of
  `release.changelog` names, and `<name>@<version>` for each workspace package
  that is not private when the version `<dir>/package.json` declares is the one
  the newest section of `<dir>/CHANGELOG.md` names. Each tag goes on the commit
  that set its version: HEAD, or, where later commits landed on the branch, the
  earlier commit, with a warning naming how many commits HEAD is past it. A unit
  whose version a tag already names is skipped. Every unit is decided before the
  first tag is written, and the run writes nothing when another branch is
  checked out, when every unit is skipped, or when any unit's two files
  disagree, its version's changelog section carries no `<!-- rafa:fragments -->`
  receipt and is above the newest version released before settle, no commit
  holds its version yet, or its version file, the tag list or the history could
  not be read. After the tags it prints what to run next: per tag, the push that
  puts it on the remote and the publish line for the registry its manifest
  configures, with the command `release.publishCommand` names (`npm publish` by
  default), run in the package's folder for a package and spelled to publish
  from the tag when HEAD is past it, which it does not run. Under
  `release.publish: ci` a unit's publish line is replaced by one sentence saying
  the pushed tag publishes through `.github/workflows/release-publish.yml`, and
  json carries `publish: "ci"` on that unit. With `--push` it pushes each tag
  itself to the remote the release branch tracks (`origin` when it tracks none)
  and drops its push line; a push that fails exits 1 with what git said and
  keeps the local tags. With `--output=json` the readings, the decisions, the
  follow-ups and the pushes of every unit are the data of the terminal result
  event.

Flags:
  --push   boolean
      Push each tag to the remote the release branch tracks once every tag is
      written; a push that fails exits 1 and keeps the local tags.

Examples:
  rafa release tag
      Tags the merged release of every unit and prints the push and publish
      lines to run next.
  rafa release tag --push
      Tags the merged release of every unit, pushes the tags, and prints the
      publish lines to run next.
  rafa release tag --output=json
      Writes the same tags and gives every unit's readings, decision and
      follow-ups as a result event.

Outputs:
  text, json

See also:
  rafa release status, rafa release settle, rafa release list
